description: A fresh explicit Off lets legacy work proceed exactly as before the module existed.

A timeout, a non-success response, a malformed or missing answer, or no module at all is unknown: no legacy read or write, a retryable 503. A response that says off with a failing HTTP status is not an Off.
Unknown first, then On: no stream answer until the On record is durable, then streams only and no legacy.

A still-fresh Off is never ended by a later answer that is not a usable explicit state: a timeout, an HTTP error, an unauthenticated reply or a malformed body changes nothing. Legacy keeps working until the Off reaches its deadline.
Once On, a later Off (fresh or stale), an unknown answer, an outage or expiry never lowers it, and legacy work stays refused.
A is On, B is Off, A signs in again: each owner keeps its own state.
Evidence, reads and commits need an owner. A missing owner, or evidence whose owner differs from the authenticated one, is unknown and changes no state for either owner.
A legacy write admitted under Off, paused, and resumed after On was latched is refused at commit; nothing is written later.
On is saved outside the data database: it survives a crash before the first commit and a wiped data database.

While the On record is not yet durable (paused or failed save), no read, admission or commit is answered as On and no legacy write is authorized. A crash in that window leaves nothing durable. A later On answer retries the save.

A stored Off is usable one millisecond before its deadline, expired exactly at it, and expired days later. A reboot with an untrusted clock expires it too. A fresh explicit Off resumes legacy work. Expiry never lowers On.

Two runtimes open one store. The first owns it. The second is refused with 503 and never admits a legacy write, not before the first latches On and not after. A record is only ever written by its owner.

The Account switches on another device while this device holds a fresh Off. Legacy commits are allowed while that Off is fresh (migration-only loss is accepted). At the first On this device observes, the module saves importPending with the On. Every answer says importRequired until the host reports importDone.
A never-seen owner gets a retryable 503 only until the first Account answer. When that answer is an explicit Off, normal legacy work proceeds with no 503.
A never-seen owner whose first answer is On reaches streams after the save, with importRequired false when the device holds no legacy files, and true when it does.

A new user's first launch: boot, the sign-in answer arrives as an explicit Off, and the first collection runs. Nothing is refused anywhere in the trace: the Off is saved before it is used, and with a working disk that save costs the user nothing.
Sign-in worked but the mode read failed on first launch: unknown is refused with a retryable 503. When the next answer is an explicit Off, the same owner proceeds.

An Off is saved before it is used, as an On is. When the save fails, the answer is unknown: nothing is admitted, read or committed on the strength of an Off that never reached the disk. A later Off that saves restores normal legacy work.

The first On is saved with importPending. The process dies before the host hears the answer. After the restart every answer still says an import is owed, and stream commits are refused with 503 IMPORT_PENDING. Legacy stays refused with 426.
importDone is saved before it is used. Once saved, stream commits pass and importRequired is false, also after a restart. An importDone for an owner with no pending import changes nothing.
An Off whose fetch started more than 60 s after the module's wall clock is unknown evidence: it creates no record and refuses legacy. A fetch start 59 s ahead is clamped to age zero and counts.

While the import is pending, an ordinary stream commit gets 503 IMPORT_PENDING and the importer's seed publish for the same owner is admitted. The seed publish is admitted again after a crash, still pending. After importDone ordinary commits pass. A seed publish for an owner the module has no On for is not admitted.
